package.title: The Cholesterol Number You Can Calculate Yourself #shorts
package.description:
New EASD 2026 data on 313,145 adults with overweight or obesity (no heart disease or diabetes) suggests two blood markers, remnant cholesterol and hs-CRP, may flag a rise in coronary heart disease risk that looks similar, in relative terms, to people who qualify for GLP-1s, even at a BMI of 25–26.9, below today's usual cutoff. Early, observational conference data; links, not proof; no drugs tested. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about your own situation. #GLP1 #cholesterol #heartHealth #metabolicHealth #hsCRP

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation.

Sources:
- Medical Xpress (reporting Hvid K et al., EASD 2026 Annual Meeting, Milan): https://medicalxpress.com/news/2026-09-millions-people-overweight-benefit-glp.html
- Varbo A et al. Remnant Cholesterol as a Causal Risk Factor for Ischemic Heart Disease. JACC 2013;61(4):427-436: https://www.jacc.org/doi/abs/10.1016/j.jacc.2012.08.1026
- Pearson TA et al. Markers of inflammation and cardiovascular disease (CDC/AHA). Circulation 2003;107(3):499-511: https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1161/01.cir.0000052939.59093.45
- FDA. FDA Approves New Drug Treatment for Chronic Weight Management, First Since 2014 (2021): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USFDA/bulletins/2e2adc7

social.facebook_caption:
Your cholesterol test might already have a heart-risk clue hiding in it — and it's easy to overlook.

Researchers presenting at EASD 2026 looked at 313,145 adults with overweight or obesity who didn't have heart disease or diabetes, focusing on those with a BMI of 25 to 26.9 — below the usual cutoff for weight-management GLP-1 medicines. About half of them had high remnant cholesterol, low-grade inflammation (measured by hs-CRP), or both, and the rise in their coronary heart disease risk looked similar (in relative terms) to that seen in people who currently qualify for GLP-1s.

Remnant cholesterol can be estimated from a standard lipid panel (total cholesterol minus LDL minus HDL), and hs-CRP is an inflammation blood test linked to heart disease risk. Worth flagging: this is early conference data, it's observational (a link, not proof), and no treatment was tested here.

Have you ever had these two markers checked?

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation.

#GLP1 #HeartHealth #Cholesterol

There's a heart-risk number hiding in your regular cholesterol panel 👀

New data presented at EASD 2026 looked at 313,145 adults with overweight or obesity, no heart disease, no diabetes — focused on a BMI of 25 to 26.9, which is under today's usual cutoff for weight-management GLP-1s.

Roughly half had high remnant cholesterol, low-grade inflammation (measured by hs-CRP), or both. In this group, the rise in coronary heart disease risk looked similar (in relative terms) to people who currently qualify for GLP-1s.

Two markers worth knowing:

→ hs-CRP: an inflammation blood test linked to heart disease risk

Important: this is early conference data, it's observational (links, not proof), and no treatment was tested in this study.

Save this for your next doctor's visit, and bring up both markers.

script.cta: GLP-1s aren't approved for weight management at a BMI of 25–26.9 today. This is early, observational conference data, and no drugs were tested. Ask your doctor about remnant cholesterol and hs-CRP, and talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether any treatment is right for you. Full breakdown on our channel: "Not 'Heavy Enough' for a GLP-1? Two Blood Markers That May Matter More Than BMI". Follow @InforMedLab.

factcheck.summary:
All four sources exist and mostly support the script. src1 (Medical Xpress on Hvid K et al., EASD 2026, Milan, 28 Sep–2 Oct 2026) confirms: 313,145 adults with BMI ≥25 from the UK Biobank and Copenhagen General Population Study, with no coronary heart disease or diabetes at baseline. It also confirms that 44% (CGPS) and 48% (UK Biobank) of people with BMI 25–26.9 had high remnant cholesterol, low-grade inflammation or both. The outcome was coronary heart disease, the design was observational, and the authors say trials are needed. src4 (the FDA Wegovy 2021 announcement) confirms the eligibility cutoff: BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a weight-related condition. src2 (Varbo 2013 JACC 61:427-436) and src3 (Pearson 2003 Circulation 107:499-511) exist and support the remnant cholesterol calculation and hs-CRP as a heart-risk marker.

One major framing error in s4: the 'similar risk rise' finding (41% higher in CGPS, 47% higher in UK Biobank, versus 41% and 35% for people who already qualify for GLP-1s, all compared with people with healthy levels) applies only to people with BOTH elevated remnant cholesterol AND low-grade inflammation. Right after s3's 'or both', the line 'people with those markers' tells viewers that having either marker alone carries that risk. A few minor precision fixes are listed too. The caveats, clinician line and CTA are good. No dosing, no prescribing advice, no unsafe content.

issues.claim: for people with those markers, the rise in coronary heart disease risk looked similar to people who qualify for GLP-1s today
issues.problem: The source says the similar risk rise (41%/47% higher vs 41%/35% for people who already qualify, each compared with people with healthy cholesterol and inflammation levels) was for people with elevated remnant cholesterol AND low-grade inflammation together. Coming straight after s3's 'or both', 'those markers' implies that either marker alone carries this risk. That overgeneralizes the finding.
issues.fix: Narration: "Here's the twist: for people with BOTH markers, the rise in coronary heart disease risk looked similar to people who qualify for GLP-1s today." On-screen: "Both markers: risk rise looked similar (relative)"

issues.problem: The exclusion was coronary heart disease at baseline, not all heart disease. It's a small overgeneralization of the study population.
issues.fix: Narration: "...adults with overweight or obesity, and no coronary heart disease or diabetes..." stat_label: "adults, BMI 25+, no coronary heart disease or diabetes"

issues.problem: The range is two separate cohort figures (44% CGPS, 48% UK Biobank), not a confidence range. It needs a qualifier line saying what it counts.
issues.fix: stat_label: "of people with BMI 25–26.9 had high remnant cholesterol, low-grade inflammation or both (44% Danish cohort, 48% UK Biobank)"

issues.claim: Estimate it from a standard lipid panel: total cholesterol, minus LDL, minus HDL.
issues.problem: This is accurate as an estimate (the Varbo 2013 method), but without a threshold viewers can't tell what counts as 'high'. Add a pointer to the clinician so viewers don't self-interpret.
issues.fix: "Marker one: remnant cholesterol. Estimate it from a standard lipid panel: total cholesterol, minus LDL, minus HDL. Your doctor can tell you what your number means."

hold_reason: Dropped by Editor-in-Chief: A major factual error is still unfixed. The video (s4) and every caption say people with high remnant cholesterol, inflammation 'or both' had a risk rise similar to people who qualify for GLP-1s, but the source shows this only for people with BOTH markers. The TikTok and Threads captions also wrongly make the whole 313,145-adult cohort sound like it was BMI 25–26.9. To republish, change s4 and all captions to 'both markers' and fix the BMI wording.

audio.soundNotes: Music sits at -14dB under voice already (in target); trimmed the multiplier slightly (0.85) to bring rowdier pause moments closer to the -14dB pause target without pushing under-speech below -16dB. Pulled down a handful of cue clusters that were reading louder than the voice during speech (i20, i50, i51, i57) and thinned three overlapping tick/swoosh layers in dense clusters (i12, i17, i45, i71, i73) so no more than 3-4 effects land in any one second. Boosted the pause-only whip at the first stat reveal (i4) and the outro swell/whoosh (i81/i82) slightly for a stronger punctuation on the big reveal and the brand close. Added four bespoke SFX (heartbeat, two clinical marker shimmers, outro sting) to reinforce key story beats the stock kit doesn't cover, all kept low and felt rather than heard over narration.
